title: Infection Risk and Reimbursement in Ambulatory Cystoscopy: Comparing Single-Use and Reusable Scopes
summary:
This study investigates whether the risk of urinary tract infections after a bladder examination differs between single-use and reusable devices.

Cystoscopy is a common procedure performed in urology practices. During the procedure, a thin instrument is inserted through the urethra into the bladder. Reusable devices are cleaned and disinfected after use, often using manual processes that may vary in practice.

Single-use devices, on the other hand, are sterile and used only once.

In this study, patients are randomly assigned to one of two groups: examination with a single-use device or a reusable device. Before the procedure, urine is tested to rule out an existing infection.

After the procedure, symptoms, possible infections, hospitalizations, and treatments are recorded. In addition, the costs associated with the procedure and any follow-up care are analyzed.

The aim of the study is to determine whether single-use devices reduce the risk of infections and to assess their impact on patient care and healthcare costs.
conditions: Investigation of urinary tract infections following diagnostic cystoscopy in an outpatient setting

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Existing indication for a planned diagnostic cystoscopy
- Signed and dated patient informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Medical or psychological conditions associated with impaired capacity to consent or that preclude participation in the study
- Patients with pre-existing symptomatic or asymptomatic bacteriuria (nitrite-positive)
- Presence of urinary tract implants or catheters (increased risk of infection)
- Non-retractable phimosis
- Severe urethral fibrosis/strictures
- Ongoing antibiotic therapy
